entries: Hazard identification and assessment｜Inspecting workplaces, equipment, and work methods, identifying chemical, physical, biological, and ergonomic hazards, and assessing exposure and risk.

Program and procedure design｜Designing and maintaining occupational health and safety programs, such as noise surveys, continuous air monitoring, ventilation assessment, dust and chemical management, and medical surveillance plans.
Inspection and compliance｜Inspecting sites and equipment for conformity with safety standards and regulations, identifying non-conformities, and requiring correction.

Sampling and testing｜Collecting dust, gas, vapor, or other toxic substance samples and arranging analysis, and checking working conditions such as ventilation and lighting that affect health and performance.
Accident investigation and data analysis｜Investigating accidents and health complaints to determine causes, and analyzing incident data to identify trends in injuries, illnesses, and hazards.
Training and emergency response｜Conducting safety training and new-employee health and safety induction training, and maintaining emergency plans and response procedures.

Collaboration and escalation｜Working with engineers, physicians, and managers to develop control or corrective measures, and recommending suspension of threatening operations and reporting upward when necessary.

rows.label: Inspection and compliance judgment
rows.value: Check whether the site, equipment, and work conform to safety standards and government regulations, identify non-conformities, and require correction

rows.label: Sampling and testing arrangements
rows.value: Collect dust, gas, vapor, and other toxic substance samples and arrange analysis, and check conditions affecting health such as ventilation and lighting

rows.label: Accident investigation and trend analysis
rows.value: Investigate accidents and health complaints to determine causes, and analyze incident data to identify trends in injuries, illnesses, and hazards

rows.label: Training and emergency preparedness
rows.value: Conduct safety training and new-employee induction training, and maintain or update emergency plans and response procedures

rows.label: Collaboration and suspension recommendations
rows.value: Work with engineers and physicians to develop control or corrective measures, and recommend suspending threatening operations when necessary

signals.body: You are willing to go on site to verify hazards and protection, and can map observations and monitoring data to regulatory requirements and write them as traceable records.
signals.label: Fit signals

signals.body: You find it hard to face on-site exposure and noise over the long term, or tend to skip verification and escalation under accident and conflict pressure.
signals.label: Caution signals

signals.body: A 60-minute fully fictional paper-based ABC, without entering the site or contacting chemicals. A: workshop S01 has grinding dust and noise and cleaning fluid X; the composition/SDS, exposure time, and applicable standards are not given. B: at 09:00 the noise reading shows 88dB, and the instrument calibration, measurement settings, and sampling duration are unknown; sample sheet S10, site S01, with no monitoring report attached. C: the ventilation maintenance record lacks a review signature, and the manager asks for a statement that everything meets standards and work can resume. Submit a three-column table of facts—unknowns—verification owners, plus a handover draft, and do not create a real monitoring or equipment operation plan. Reference: the three groups to verify are dust/noise exposure, the unknown cleaning fluid, and ventilation and review; 88 is only the raw display and cannot be used for a compliance judgment against a limit value that was not given. S01/S10 does not automatically mean the same site; a missing review signature must not be filled in. The conclusion is that evidence is insufficient and no compliance or return-to-work certificate is issued; a real immediate threat should be handed to authorized personnel promptly per the institutional emergency procedure, without waiting for the seven-day exercise to end.
